Who writes the grading rubric when a question has no single correct answer?

Xiaohongshu and Fudan University introduce DR-Rubric, a study reported as accepted to NeurIPS 2026.

The bottleneck: Generic instructions such as "be clear and complete" miss the facts and constraints that make a particular answer useful. Training against a weak rubric can reward the wrong behavior.

The mechanism: An agent first researches the question, collecting external evidence and likely failure modes. It converts that evidence into individually checkable constraints, then uses the fraction satisfied as a reinforcement-learning reward. A bootstrapping stage lets the trained model generate rubrics for later rounds.

The payoff: With 1,000 RL instances after a shared Qwen3-8B-SFT initialization, the GPT-5-rubric variant scores 73.7 on ResearchQA and 43.0 on DeepResearchBench, 3.8 and 3.2 points above the best listed baselines. Bootstrapping is not reliably monotonic: later rounds can increase internal rewards while degrading real task performance.
